explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full slack system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Slack clone demonstrates a functional multi-page flow with clear pricing differentiation and successful form validation states. However, the mobile experience is severely compromised by pervasive accessibility violations, specifically touch targets that are significantly smaller than the recommended 44px minimum across navigation, forms, and critical recovery links. Additionally, several high-value interactive elements, such as SSO buttons and demo links, appear to be non-functional placeholders, creating dead ends in the user journey.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the Slack marketing site, focusing on the pricing decision flow, feature discovery, and conversion paths (Sign Up/Sales), while validating mobile responsiveness against known layout warnings.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will begin by validating the primary navigation and hero section on the homepage. It will then dive deep into the Pricing page to test plan comparison logic and billing toggles. Subsequent phases will cover Feature discovery, Enterprise/Trust validation, and the 'Talk to Sales' lead generation form. The run concludes with a mobile viewport pass to verify tap targets flagged in the prescan.
assumptions: The 'Get started free' flow leads to a functional email capture or OAuth simulation on get-started.html.
The 'Talk to sales' form on contact.html accepts dummy data for submission testing.
Anchor links on features.html (e.g., #channels) correctly scroll to or display specific module details.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Monthly/Annual toggle state persistence and price updates.
pricing.html: Feature comparison table readability and alignment.
contact.html: Form validation errors and required field handling.
Mobile Viewport: Navigation menu accessibility and small tap targets (identified in prescan).

phases.title: Homepage & Navigation Baseline
phases.objective: Validate global navigation consistency and primary hero CTAs.
key_checks: Verify all top-level nav links (Features, Solutions, Enterprise, Pricing) resolve correctly.
Test 'Get started free' CTA redirection to get-started.html.
Test 'Talk to sales' CTA redirection to contact.html.
Scroll through product modules (Channels, AI, Automation) to check for lazy-loading issues or broken animations.

phases.title: Pricing Logic & Comparison
phases.objective: Deep dive into the pricing structure, toggles, and plan differentiation.
key_checks: Toggle between 'Monthly' and 'Annual' billing; verify price updates and discount messaging.
Scan the feature comparison table for visual alignment and clarity.
Click 'Get started free' under different tiers to ensure consistent redirection.
Check FAQ accordion interactions for expand/collapse functionality.
exit_criteria: Billing toggle state changes reflected in UI.

phases.title: Feature Discovery & Enterprise Trust
phases.objective: Explore detailed feature pages and enterprise-specific trust signals.
key_checks: On features.html: Click category tabs (Collaboration, Project Management, etc.) to filter content.
Test anchor links from index.html (e.g., 'Learn more about Channels') land on correct sections.
On enterprise.html: Verify security badges and compliance info visibility.
On trust.html: Check for clear hierarchy of security information.

phases.title: Conversion Flows (Sales & Sign Up)
phases.objective: Test the lead generation and account creation forms.
key_checks: On contact.html: Fill out 'Talk to sales' form with valid dummy data; test submit behavior.
On contact.html: Attempt submit with missing required fields to check validation UI.
On get-started.html: Test email input and 'Continue' button.
On signin.html: Verify 'Forgot password' and SSO options (Google/Microsoft) are present.
exit_criteria: Success state or next step visible on valid submission.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport to address prescan warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/Pixel 5).
Verify hamburger menu opens and closes correctly.
Re-test tap targets for Nav links and Pricing toggles (previously flagged as <44px).
Ensure pricing tables stack or scroll horizontally without breaking layout.
Check form inputs on contact.html for zoom/focus issues.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise billing toggles, feature filters, form validations, and accordions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Full pass on Homepage, Pricing, and Contact pages.

notes: Prescan identified multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings on index.html; prioritize checking these in Phase 5.
No backend connectivity is expected; focus on frontend UI states and redirection logic.
Keep an eye on the 'AI' feature mentions across pages to ensure consistent messaging.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site and interact with controls on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Critical touch targets are significantly below the 44px mobile accessibility guideline, making interaction difficult or impossible for touch users.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag the 'Sign in' button (41px height), 'Create an account' link (17px height), 'Forgot your password?' link (17px height), and global navigation links (23px height) as too small. The billing toggle on the pricing page is also only 24px high.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will experience high friction and frequent mis-taps. Links with 17px heights are effectively unclickable for average finger sizes, blocking access to account creation and password recovery.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and min-height of all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs, toggles) to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px, even if the visual label remains smaller.
findings.source_hint: signin.html: ux-4, ux-7, ux-8; pricing.html: billing toggle

findings.user_goal: Reset a forgotten password using the mobile interface.
findings.problem: The native browser validation tooltip obscures the submit button when the email field is left empty, preventing immediate correction.
findings.evidence: In step agentic-77-click, clicking 'Send reset link' with an empty email field triggered a native 'Please fill out this field' tooltip that positioned itself directly over the 'Send reset link' button.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates a confusing loop where the error message blocks the very control needed to dismiss it or re-submit. Users may feel stuck or forced to scroll/zoom to resolve the state.
findings.suggestion: Implement custom inline validation messages that appear below the input field rather than relying solely on native tooltips that can obscure UI elements. Ensure the error state does not block the primary action button.

findings.user_goal: Log in using a corporate Google or Microsoft account.
findings.problem: SSO buttons ('Sign in with Google/Microsoft') and secondary CTAs ('Watch demo') appear clickable but function as dead links/placeholders.
findings.evidence: Steps agentic-73-78 and steps-55-60 confirm that clicking these buttons results in no URL change, no modal opening, and no visible state update. The 'Watch demo' link on enterprise.html points to '#'.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks user trust and causes confusion. Users expect these prominent buttons to initiate an authentication flow or open a video player. Dead ends increase bounce rates and frustration.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the full functionality for these high-priority features or visually disable them (greyed out, removed) if they are not yet ready, to avoid misleading users.
findings.source_hint: signin.html: ux-5, ux-6; enterprise.html: Watch demo

findings.user_goal: Browse specific feature categories (e.g., AI, Integrations) on the Features page.
findings.problem: Tab navigation relies on hash-based scrolling which fails silently on mobile viewports for certain sections.
findings.evidence: In step agentic-67-72, clicking the 'Intelligence' tab on mobile failed to navigate to the '#ai' anchor, leaving the viewport stuck on the previous section. The tool reported 'changed: false' and the screenshot confirmed the content did not update.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access key content sections, leading to the assumption that the information is missing. Inconsistent behavior between desktop (where it worked via scroll) and mobile degrades the responsive experience.
findings.suggestion: Ensure anchor IDs exist for all target sections in the mobile DOM. Consider using JavaScript-driven scroll-to-element logic with offset adjustments for fixed headers to guarantee reliable navigation across all viewports.

findings.user_goal: Understand the cost difference between monthly and annual billing.
findings.problem: While the price updates correctly, the visual feedback for the 'Annual' discount could be more prominent to drive conversion.
findings.evidence: The 'Save up to 18%' badge is visible, but the price change (e.g., Pro from $8.75 to $7.25) happens without a strong animation or strikethrough of the old price to emphasize the savings magnitude.
findings.why_it_matters: Subtle changes may be missed by users scanning the page. Emphasizing the savings more aggressively can nudge users toward the higher-commitment annual plan.
findings.suggestion: Add a strikethrough effect to the monthly price when annual is selected, or animate the price drop to draw attention to the value proposition.
